what: Written before the JavaScript version of three checks is compared with the Python version. The page web/try.html runs moving, shapes and untrusted in the browser on a pasted diff. Does it say exactly what the Python job says?
data: (A) The 4,451 agent-written commits with a patch in the cached AIDev rows (eval/cache/aidev/commit_details.json), as file rows. (B) 400 Mesa commits chosen with the seed 20261018 from 2024-01-01 to 2026-09-30, read as raw `git show` diffs so the page's own diff reader is included. (C) The example diffs on the page itself (web/try_examples.json). This line was changed from 'the unit-test fixtures' before any comparison was run, because the page's examples are what a visitor will actually paste. (D) Added in this file before the registered run, because the checks speak on well under 1% of real commits and agreement on silent commits is weak evidence: a line corpus. Candidate lines are every string of 6 to 300 characters in tests/test_moving.py, tests/test_shapes.py and tests/test_untrusted.py, plus up to 6,000 added lines from the AIDev rows and the 400 Mesa commits that contain one of: curl, wget, base64, eval, atob, environ, process.env, ${{, CI_, image:, FROM, ref:, remote:, component:, writeFile, fetch(, download. Lines are put in groups of 6 as the added lines of one synthetic file, once under each of these paths: .github/workflows/x.yml, .gitlab-ci.yml, Dockerfile, scripts/x.sh, src/x.ts.
unit: One commit (or one fixture): the list of what each check names, as (path, line, kind, text) in order. For (D) one unit is one synthetic file.
rule: Agreement means the two lists are identical for every unit and every check. Met only if there is no disagreement. Every disagreement is published with its commit id prefix, the check and both answers (no diff text). The Python is the reference: a disagreement is fixed in the JavaScript, and the run is repeated and published with both runs.
limits: Agreement says the two programs behave alike, not that either is right: how often the checks speak and what they catch is in results/mesa_noise_v1.json, results/agent_noise_v1.json and results/incident_replay_v1.json.
v2: After the v1 run (all identical; results/try_agreement_v1.json) a mutation check of the JavaScript showed that the v1 corpora never exercised deleted files, files under docs/ or tests/, .py and .bash paths, or the trailer of a format-patch mail, so six deliberate breaks of the JavaScript went unnoticed. The v2 run adds those cases (the same rule) and is published beside v1.
